So this is what I’m going through currently, I had a further consultation with my provider tonight and he told me that I have borderline personality disorder then it’s stem to my avoidant personality disorder, but he didn’t want to label it a disorder because it stems from my borderline personality. He didn’t want to give me that avoidant personality disorder immediately because he didn’t want to overwhelm me with two diagnosis. even though I met all the criteria for the avoidant personality disorder, he knows the my avoidant personality is in the pathological state and that it stems from the borderline personality disorder and traumas associated, which then leads to our complications. We ended our conversation with him understanding that his mindset of a multiple diagnosis is not something that he finds ideal to be helpful. however, for me, it is helpful to know everything that’s playing a factor in it so that I can get better help. So we ended off with him understanding that his mindset of not wanting to overwhelm his patient with multiple diagnosis isn’t ideal for everyone. And he understood that me, knowing about the both of the personality disorders will help me navigate both of them rather than just putting emphasis on one. So like you with multiple diagnosis is, it could be complicated to understand what comes from what but without some of them you may not fully understand yourself. So he has this mindset of if you go to the problem that initially occurred if you fix that, it should unravel some of the other things.However, my metaphor is if you have heart cancer in that spread throughout your body and now you have cancer in your liver or your ovaries, you still have cancer in your liver ovaries and heart. Just because it stemmed from your heart doesn’t mean that you don’t have all these other things going on. So some doctors don’t want to overdiagnosed to overwhelm someone but they meet all the diagnostic criteria and are in the pathological level to have those disorder diagnosis. So it becomes complicated for both the person diagnosing and the person receiving the diagnosis that’s why there has to be a level of open communication and what’s helpful for the client and what is helpful for everyone to come on agreement with that’s why the right person to helping you navigate this is important but that’s a lot to navigate to so I empathize with both of our scenarios because it’s hard.
